title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Kernel Scheduling, Profiling Playbook, Benchmarking Suite, Runbooks, and Known Issues
author: Priya Desai
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the authoritative reference for the Redwood serving runtime: architecture, kernel scheduling strategy, profiling and benchmarking playbooks, runbooks for common operational tasks and incidents, release notes summary for the current release line (v3.x), and the curated list of known issues with mitigation guidance. It is intended for engineers owning the runtime, SREs, and platform integrators.

Goals
- Provide a single source of truth for runtime components, responsibilities, and SLOs.
- Document reproducible profiling and benchmarking procedures used by the performance team.
- Give on-call runbooks and escalation paths for critical incidents.
- Surface known issues, workarounds, and tracking tickets.

Audience and ownership
- Primary owners: eng-serving-runtime (runtime infra), eng-sre for SLOs and alerting.
- Document steward: Priya Desai (runtime tech lead).
- Review cadence: quarterly or on major release.

1) Runtime architecture (high level)

Summary:
The serving runtime (service name: runtime-service) provides token-level inference for models hosted on Redwood’s Dedicated and Hosted deployments. Core components:
- Inference proxy (inference-proxy): handles HTTP/ gRPC surface, authentication, and request routing.
- Batcher (continuous-batcher): accumulates requests up to per-model batch_size and latency deadline.
- Scheduler (kernel-scheduler): assigns batches to GPU workers using cost & latency-aware heuristics.
- Worker (inference-worker): executes model kernels; manages KV cache and quantized kernels.
- KV cache (kv-cache): prefix caching service sharded per-model and region.
- Telemetry pipeline (metrics-agent -> pushgateway -> prometheus): captures latency, throughput, GPU utilization, and per-token cost breakdowns.

Key interfaces:
- API: /v1/generate (POST) — supports streaming and non-streaming.
- Admin: /internal/model-status, /internal/kv-cache/stats, /internal/scheduler/queue

SLOs & Targets (global defaults)
- Median p99 latency (request completed) — 90ms median for short-chat (<=64 tokens), 250ms p99
- Token throughput utilization: target 65–80% GPU TFLOPs on steady-state 
- Error rate: <0.05% 5xx errors across hosted fleet
- Cold-start: <150ms additional latency for warmed workers, up to 1s for cold start

2) Kernel scheduling (design and heuristics)

Design principles:
- Latency-first for interactive tiers (PLG-hosted, low-latency dedicated lanes).
- Cost-aware packing for batch/throughput tiers (dedicated reserved capacity).
- Predictable tail-latency via deadline-aware preemption and prioritized queues.

Core heuristics used by kernel-scheduler:
- Sequence-length bucketing: requests are grouped into 4 buckets: S (<=64), M (65-256), L (257-1024), XL (>1024). This minimizes padding waste when selecting kernels.
- Kernel selection table: a per-model matrix (architecture x sequence bucket x hardware) that maps to preferred kernel variant (e.g., fused-attn-v2, aten-quant-int8). The table is updated by the perf-team after each benchmark run.
- Cost function for placement: score = alpha * estimated_latency + beta * (1 - gpu_utilization) + gamma * memory_headroom_penalty. Default weights: alpha=0.6, beta=0.3, gamma=0.1.
- Deadline-aware batching: each request carries a deadline (deadline = arrival_ts + max_latency configured per route). The batcher flushes when the earliest request in the batch is within 30% of its budget.

Preemption & Fallbacks:
- Preempt long-running XL batches when interactive S-tier load exceeds 70% of latency SLOs. Preemption policy attempts graceful draining and writes partial KV cache state to stable storage.
- Fallback model routes: scheduler will route to a smaller/quantized variant if primary kernels are overloaded or incompatible; fallback decision is logged in trace id.

3) Profiling playbook (step-by-step)

Purpose:
Produce reproducible profiles to diagnose CPU/GPU hot paths, kernel inefficiencies, memory fragmentation, and KV cache hit/miss behavior.

Prerequisites:
- Access: runtime-service metrics & tracing, GPU host SSH via bastion, perf-tooling role.
- Tools: nsys (NVIDIA Nsight Systems), ncu (NVIDIA Nsight Compute), py-spy, pprof, flamegraph, bpftrace.

Procedure:
1. Baseline capture
   - Step: capture a 60s production-like sample under a synthetic workload that mirrors target distribution (use loadgen).
   - Command: ./tools/loadgen --model gpt-medium --seq-dist seed=prod-2027-03 --rps 120 --duration 60s --route interactive
   - Expected output: p95 latency within 10% of production metrics.

2. GPU timeline (nsys)
   - Command: sudo nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=profile.nsys ./bin/runtime-bench --config bench-config.yaml
   - Inspect: GPU kernel launch latency, kernel occupancy, memcpy durations. Look for serialized memcpy-copy patterns and low SM efficiency.

3. Kernel-level metrics (ncu)
   - Command: sudo ncu --target-processes all ./bin/inference-worker --model gpt-medium --batch 8
   - Inspect: achieved FLOPs, memory throughput, L2 cache hit rates. Compare against golden baseline for model & hardware.

4. Python & CPU sampling
   - Command: py-spy record -o profile.svg -- python -m runtime_worker.main --trace-id=local-1234
   - Inspect: event loop stalls, serialization overhead, batching logic hotspots.

5. KV cache analysis
   - Query: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://internal.kv-cache/service/stats?model=gpt-medium
   - Metrics: hit_rate, eviction_rate, avg_ttl_ms. Target hit_rate > 75% for interactive routes.

6. End-to-end flamegraph
   - Generate aggregated flamegraphs and annotate with trace ids. Store artifacts under s3://redwood-perf/profiles/<date>/

Expected artifacts to attach to ticket:
- nsys .qdrep, ncu report, py-spy svg, flamegraph.svg, bench-config.yaml used, raw metrics dump (prometheus format).

4) Benchmarking suite (reproducible configs and examples)

Purpose:
Automated suite used by perf-team and release engineers to validate performance regressions and to update the kernel selection table. Benchmarks are runnable locally (via Docker) or on a dedicated perf cluster.

Key benchmark types:
- Microbench: single-kernel throughput & latency 
- Throughput-run: steady-state token-per-second at target utilization
- Tail-latency-run: simulated mixed load to measure p99 end-to-end
- Cold-start-run: measure worker init times (model load & JIT warmup)

Sample bench-config.yaml:
---
model: gpt-medium
sequence_profile: prod-2027-03
routes:
  - name: interactive
    rps: 200
    seq_bucket_weights: {S:0.6, M:0.25, L:0.1, XL:0.05}
    streaming: true
    deadline_ms: 250
worker_config:
  batch_size: 8
  max_batch_latency_ms: 40
  kernel_variant: auto
output:
  s3_bucket: s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/2027-11-15/
---

Running benchmarks (example):
- Local Docker: ./tools/bench-run --config bench-config.yaml --docker
- Perf cluster: ./tools/bench-run --config bench-config.yaml --cluster perf-cluster-us-west2 --artifacts s3://...

Pass/fail criteria:
- No regression > 5% median latency vs baseline (baseline is last-stable tag in perf registry).
- p99 must not degrade by >10% or exceed absolute thresholds in SLO table.
- Kernel selection re-eval required when bandwidth or FLOPs differ by >8% vs baseline.

5) Release notes (v3.4.x — summary)

v3.4.2 (2027-11-10) — patch
- Fix: memory leak in attention cache when using fused-attn-v2 on quantized INT8 profiles (PR #4217).
- Improvement: batcher now exposes per-batch trace id for faster triage.
- Known limitations fixed: reduced KV cache evictions under heavy mixed traffic.

v3.4.0 (2027-09-30) — minor
- Feature: deadline-aware preemption implemented in kernel-scheduler (config flag: scheduler.preempt.enabled).
- Perf: new kernel variants (aten-quant-int8) added for A100 and H100 hardware.
- Observability: added per-request cost breakdown metric runtime.request.unit_cost{gpu,mem,io}.

Upgrade guidance:
1. Canary on 5% of traffic with scheduler.preempt.enabled=true and kernel_variant=auto.
2. Monitor dashboards: runtime.latency.p99(route=interactive), scheduler.preempt.count, kv-cache.hit_rate.
3. Roll forward at 10% increments with 30-minute stabilization windows.

6) Known issues (active)

- Issue: Intermittent p99 spikes on H100 when serving XL sequences (>2048).
  - Symptom: p99 increases by 2-3x for 5–15 minute windows, GPUs show low SM efficiency.
  - Root cause (investigation): kernel fusion mis-selects non-fused kernel under certain memory fragmentation patterns.
  - Mitigation: set model override kernel_variant=fused-attn-v2 for affected models and add scheduler rule to route XL sequences to dedicated throughput lane.
  - Tracking: TICKET-8931

- Issue: KV cache eviction storms during autoscaling events.
  - Symptom: hit_rate drops below 40% for several minutes after scale-in.
  - Mitigation: enable sticky-cache-affinity: true in kv-cache config and increase eviction grace window to 120s.
  - Tracking: TICKET-9075

- Issue: Occasionally the batcher yields empty-batch flushes causing high small-batch overheads.
  - Symptom: elevated per-token cost & increased CPU syscalls.
  - Mitigation: bump max_batch_latency_ms to 60ms for routes with >50% S traffic while we deploy batching improvements.
  - Tracking: TICKET-9182

7) Runbooks & playbooks (operational procedures)

A. Incident: p99 latency spike (interactive route)
1. Triage (0-5m)
   - Check dashboards: runtime.latency.p99, runtime.errors.
   - Identify impacted regions/routes and correlation with autoscaling or deploys.
   - Run: curl -s "https://internal.runtime-service/internal/scheduler/queue?route=interactive" | jq
2. Immediate mitigations (5-15m)
   - If scheduler shows preemptions > 0 and latency still high -> disable preemption: curl -XPOST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" https://internal.runtime-service/admin/config -d '{"scheduler":{"preempt":{"enabled":false}}}'
   - If KV cache hit_rate < 60% -> increase sticky affinity: PATCH /internal/kv-cache/config
3. Recovery & validation (15-60m)
   - Gradually scale up interactive capacity (kubernetes: kubectl scale deployment/runtime-worker --replicas=<n>).
   - Validate: runtime.latency.p95 returns to baseline and p99 decreases exponentially.
4. Post-incident
   - Open postmortem: template in /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/postmortems-template. Include artifacts produced in profiling playbook.

B. Incident: GPU OOM on inference-worker
1. Triage
   - Pull worker logs and dmesg on host.
   - Query allocator: /internal/worker/allocations?host=<host-id>
2. Mitigation
   - Drain worker: POST /internal/worker/drain?host=<host-id> -> scale replacement nodes.
   - Temporarily route large-seq to smaller model variant or move to CPU fallback lane.
3. Fix
   - Increase memory headroom configured for kernel_variant or rebuild model with lower max_context.

C. Routine: Update kernel selection table
1. Owner: perf-team 
2. Steps:
   - Run microbench & throughput-run for model+hardware combinations.
   - Validate metrics and produce a delta report vs baseline.
   - Submit PR to infra-configs/kernel-selection.yaml with new variant and justification.
   - Tag the release and schedule rollout via canary.

8) Observability & dashboards (what to watch)
- runtime.latency.{p50,p95,p99} by route and model
- runtime.request.unit_cost{gpu,mem,io} by route
- scheduler.queue_depth and scheduler.preempt.count
- kv-cache.hit_rate, kv-cache.evictions_per_min
- worker.gpu_utilization, worker.sm_efficiency, worker.mem_used_mb

9) Team wiki & knowledge base pointers
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/serving-runtime-reference-2027-03-04 (reference architecture)
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/serving-runtime-ops-and-playbook-2027-08-15 (ops playbook)
- s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/ (benchmark artifacts)
- Git repos: git.internal.redwood.com/infra/runtime, git.internal.redwood.com/perf/loadgen

10) Change log & next milestones
- 2027-11-15: v3.4.2 patch (see release notes section).
- Planned: kernel-selection auto-tuner (Q1 2028), improved sticky-cache sharding (Q1 2028), batching protocol v2 (Q2 2028).

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets & templates
- Dump scheduler queue
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://internal.runtime-service/internal/scheduler/queue?format=json | jq '.'

- Example admin toggles (use only with owner approval):
  curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://internal.runtime-service/admin/config -d '{"scheduler":{"preempt":{"enabled":false}}}'

- Postmortem checklist (short):
  1) Summary & timeline
  2) Impact (customers, routes)
  3) Root cause & contributing factors
  4) Short-term mitigations & long-term fixes
  5) Action owners & deadlines

If you find missing sections or want to add runbook steps, please submit changes by creating a PR against this page (see page footer instructions) or contact the document owner.
